key_insight: EEG decoding favors word identity in early LLM layers and passage-level context in deeper layers, even from a single 0.5-second EEG window.
engineering_relevance: Target-layer selection offers a design dial for EEG language decoders, trading word-level decodability against passage-context tracking.
method: Train a separate EEG-to-embedding decoder for each Llama-3.1-8B layer.
Compare decoding with and without a causal transformer over EEG-window sequences.
Test context tracking using accuracy-calibrated synthetic predictors and within- versus across-session prediction permutations.
evidence_signal: Using 19-channel EEG during silent reading, word-level decodability peaked early and declined with layer depth, while context tracking increased; controls indicated it mostly followed the text rather than recording-session signatures.
watch_item: The abstract does not report sample size or effect sizes, limiting assessment of robustness and generalizability.
paper_title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
